plan: Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $31. This eliminates the risk of overbidding and ensures I maximize potential profit. Since values are independently drawn each round, there's no historical context to adjust my strategy. By bidding my true value, I create the best expected outcome - if I win, I'll earn the difference between my value and the second-highest bid, and if I lose, I lose nothing.

Economic theory suggests bidding exactly my true value ($11) is the dominant strategy in a second-price sealed-bid auction. Since values are independently and randomly drawn each round, there's no strategic advantage to bidding above or below my true value. I want to maximize my potential profit by winning if my value is highest, while minimizing overpayment. Bidding $11 ensures I win if my value is highest and pays only the second-highest bid.
